title: Rare illegal memory access when multiple trtexec processes use CUDA Graph
body: I rarely get `Cuda failure: an illegal memory access was encountered` when two or more `trtexec` processes run the same engine on an RTX 4090 with `--useCudaGraph --iterations=1000000`; a single process does not trigger it. Setting `CUDA_ENABLE_COREDUMP_ON_EXCEPTION=1` does not generate a CUDA dump and makes the problem harder to reproduce, while compute-sanitizer and cuda-gdb have not reproduced it so far. The initial environment is `nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:23.09-py3`. A gdb run eventually stopped after the CUDA failure with SIGABRT in `sample::cudaCheck`, called from `inferenceExecution`.

symptoms_visible: When I run two or more trtexec processes with CUDA Graph on the same RTX 4090, one can rarely print `Cuda failure: an illegal memory access was encountered`; I have not seen it with only one process.
Enabling CUDA exception coredumps produces no dump and makes the failure less likely, and my initial compute-sanitizer and cuda-gdb runs did not reproduce it.
One later gdb run reached the CUDA failure and then stopped with SIGABRT in `sample::cudaCheck` from `inferenceExecution`.
N0.label: N0 rare concurrent CUDA failure reported

symptoms_visible: The illegal-memory-access message appears only after a long concurrent run, sometimes after 10 to 20 minutes or more.
N1.label: N1 initial reproduction package shared

symptoms_visible: The first model I shared does not reproduce the failure, but the corrected test model does when I run two trtexec processes with CUDA Graph and four streams on the RTX 4090.
With the corrected case, trtexec prints the illegal-memory-access error and dmesg reports an Xid 31 MMU fault with a virtual-read fault.
N2.label: N2 corrected reproduction and GPU fault evidence

symptoms_visible: My corrected concurrent test still encounters the illegal-memory-access failure; no public workaround has been provided.
N3.label: N3 NVIDIA attributes failure to CUDA

symptoms_visible: A maintainer reports that overnight RTX 4090 testing on a newer supported CUDA stack no longer reproduces the failure; I have not retested that stack on my own system.
N_terminal.label: terminal closed after maintainer-only verification

question_patterns: Can you provide a reproducible model and the exact commands used to trigger the failure?
How many processes or streams do you run, and approximately how long does the failure take?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I can trigger it by starting two, three, or four trtexec runs on the RTX 4090; it may take 20 minutes or more. I also shared a ResNet ONNX case and ran `mpirun -np 4 trtexec --loadEngine=resnet50_1x1024x1024.trt --useCudaGraph --streams=4 --iterations=1000000 --device=1`, which can take 10 minutes or more.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I can reproduce the same illegal access immediately with one process, without CUDA Graph, on several different GPUs.
The same concurrent command reproduces after about 30 minutes rather than 10 to 20 minutes.

edges.comment: Issue comments c1-c4, reporter's RTX 4090 system: NVIDIA requested a reproducer and the reporter supplied the initial parallel commands and model link. The reporter also warned that enabling CUDA exception coredumps makes this case harder to reproduce. This first shared model was later acknowledged to be the wrong file.

question_patterns: Can you retest in an official NVIDIA container and run separate trtexec processes instead of mpirun?
Does the shared model reproduce when tested with separate processes in a clean container?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I cannot reproduce it in the official TensorRT container with the file I first sent. I checked and realized that I sent the wrong file.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The original shared model reproduces reliably in the official container with both mpirun and separate processes.

question_patterns: Please provide the corrected test model and rerun it with separate concurrent trtexec processes.
What is the exact result with the correct model and multiple standalone processes?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I shared a new test file. With that test engine I can reproduce by launching two commands like `trtexec --loadEngine=./test.trt --device=1 --useCudaGraph --iterations=10000000 --streams=4 &` at the same time.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The corrected model also runs overnight without an error when I launch four separate processes.
The corrected model reproduces with three parallel processes instead of two.

question_patterns: Which container did you use for the successful corrected reproduction?
Can you give the exact container image for the run that fails?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The corrected test reproduces for me in `nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:24.01-py3` on the RTX 4090.

edges.comment: Issue comments c9-c11, reporter's RTX 4090 system: NVIDIA's initial run used the wrong model and did not reproduce. The reporter corrected the file, switched to two standalone four-stream commands, reproduced again, and additionally posted the Xid 31 dmesg line. The dmesg fact is volunteered in N2 because the retest request did not specifically ask for it.

solution.intent: Recognize the corrected case as a CUDA defect rather than a normal TensorRT multi-process memory conflict, track it internally, and advise waiting for an officially supported CUDA stack containing the fix because the implementation details and interim workaround cannot be disclosed publicly.
solution.concrete_example: NVIDIA reproduced the corrected test and tracked it internally. Subsequent internal debugging placed the problem in CUDA. No public workaround was disclosed; customers with an NVIDIA NDA were directed to their developer-technology contact, while others were told to wait for an official CUDA release containing the fix.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the corrected commands, illegal-access output, and Xid 31 MMU-fault line. NVIDIA first reproduced that case and later stated that internal debugging placed the defect in CUDA; the undisclosed CUDA mechanism must not be invented from the public evidence.

edges.comment: Issue comments c12 and c14-c16. NVIDIA reproduced the reporter's corrected case, filed internal bug 4479712, and later gave the final accepted diagnosis that the problem is in CUDA. The reporter requested an interim avoidance method, but NVIDIA stated that its workaround details were not public.

solution.intent: Move to an officially supported TensorRT and CUDA combination containing the CUDA-side correction, then ask the affected reporter to repeat the original concurrent RTX 4090 stress test before declaring the incident resolved.
solution.concrete_example: The maintainer later tested an RTX 4090 overnight with CUDA 12.6 and could no longer reproduce the issue; TensorRT 10.4 was identified in the thread as a supported TensorRT release for that CUDA generation. The issue was closed, but the original reporter did not post a retest, so they should run the same multi-process CUDA Graph workload on a supported updated stack and report whether the illegal access or Xid 31 returns.
solution.inference_hint: The only post-fix evidence is the NVIDIA maintainer's overnight RTX 4090 run. It is not confirmation from the original affected reporter and must not be presented as such.

edges.comment: Issue comments c18-c23. A later participant asked about release availability, NVIDIA recommended a supported newer TensorRT/CUDA pairing, and the maintainer ultimately reported that an overnight RTX 4090 test with CUDA 12.6 no longer reproduced the issue. No affected reporter confirmed the result on their own system, so the terminal state records maintainer-only verification and remains unresolved from the simulated user's perspective.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final accepted diagnosis at the level publicly established by the thread: this is a CUDA defect exposed by concurrent long-running TensorRT CUDA Graph workloads, not ordinary cross-process memory sharing or a publicly explained TensorRT engine bug.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the corrected reproducer, the repeated illegal-memory-access result, NVIDIA's successful reproduction, and the Xid 31 MMU virtual-read fault; the initial non-reproduction used the wrong model and must not be treated as disproof.
Must not invent CUDA implementation details or disclose a workaround: NVIDIA explicitly stated that both were unavailable publicly.
The practical recommendation must use an officially supported TensorRT/CUDA combination containing the CUDA-side correction rather than an unsupported version mixture.
Must ask the affected reporter to repeat the original concurrent CUDA Graph stress test on the updated supported stack and must not declare user-verified resolution until that retest succeeds.
The thread's closure establishes only that a maintainer could not reproduce the issue during an overnight RTX 4090 test on the newer CUDA stack; the original reporter did not confirm the fix.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced GPU inference user who can build TensorRT engines, run long multi-process and multi-stream stress tests, use Docker, gdb, compute-sanitizer, inspect dmesg, and share reduced models, but does not have access to NVIDIA's internal CUDA diagnosis.
persona_hint.communication_style: Urgent, persistent, and cooperative; communicates in concise non-native English, posts exact commands and raw logs, corrects mistakes openly, and repeatedly asks for reproduction status and a practical workaround.
